description.narrative: Rehabilitation of Hale Hydro Power Plant in Tanga Region in Tanzania encompassing replacement of one generating unit (10,5 MW), partial renovation of the second unit plus comprehensive rehabilitation of civil, hydraulic and electromechanical equipment and the winding of Songo songo substation

Upprustning av Hale vattenkraftstation i Tanga region i Tanzania inkl byte av en generator (10,5 MW), delvis renovering av den andra generatorn, samt upprustning av utrustning och songo songo transformatorcentralen.

The main objective of the project is to provide renewable energy for poverty reduction. The specific objective is to ensure another 30-40 years power supply from the Hale hydropower station to the national grid, which includes improved overall operational and safety aspects of the hydropower plant. Hale power station is owned and operated by the national utility company Tanzania Electric Supply Company, Tanesco.

sector.narrative: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies

description.narrative:
Progress During the Reporting Period
Lot 1 Access Road and Tunnel Works: Lot 1 was taken over by the Client (TANESCO) on 13 April 2024. The contract is currently under the Defects Liability Period of 24 months, which will run until April 2026. Lot 2 Electromechanical Works (Power Station Equipment, Intake, and Substation): The Time for Completion has been extended to 30 March 2026. As of 30 September 2025, the overall project progress stands at 68.3%. Implementation activities for Lot 2 during the reporting period included the following: i. Switchgear Building: Finishing works are ongoing (80% complete). ii. Substation: Construction of the bypass line has commenced (10% complete),and installation of the earthing system is in progress (75% complete). iii. Powerhouse and Access Shaft: Welding of the access ladder is underway (30% complete), and removal of old paint on walls and floors has progressed (85% complete). iv. Headrace Tunnel (HRT) and Penstock: Cleaning works have been completed and are awaiting commencement of headrace tunnel repair works. v. Water Intake Structure: Repair works are in progress (10% complete). vi. Dam (Spillways and Piers): Sandblasting and welding works for the large and small gates are ongoing (45% complete), while rectification of the stop log slot is progressing (60% complete).
Observation and Remarks Overall, the implementation of the project is progressing well despite minor delays, with the overall rehabilitation progress reaching 84%. According to the progress report, it is important to note that the Lot 2 Contractor has completed most of the basic design documents and equipment designs. The Client (TANESCO), with support from the Technical Assistance (TA) Consultant SWECO, is closely monitoring the contractors design work to ensure all designs are finalized on schedule, thereby enabling the timely commencement of manufacturing for the remaining equipment.
Lot 1 is currently under the Defects Liability Period following its takeover on 13 April 2024, while Lot 2 continues with the rehabilitation of existing equipment and the installation of new equipment at the powerhouse and substation. This includes finalizing the construction of the new switchgear building at the substation. The Lot 2 contract is expected to run until March 2026.
Planned Work for the Next Period: Lot 1: Continues under the defect liability period following the April 13, 2024, handover. Lot 2: Renovation of intake gate equipment Installation of new equipment at the power station and substation and Construction of a new switchgear system at the substation. The contract completion for Lot 2 remains set for August 30, 2025, but proactive measures are required to address delays and ensure timely delivery.
In summary, the project is progressing well and remains on a broadly positive trajectory. While the objectives are achievable within the intervention period, this will depend on maintaining momentum in the remaining works, particularly electromechanical installation and system integration and actively managing emerging risks over the final implementation phase.
